0.0.n: Used here as a friendly opening rather than an answer to a question.

0.2.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

0.4.n: Part of the English channel name, not a separate Japanese word.

0.6.n: Completes the English name The Game Gallery.

0.8.n: This borrowed English word identifies The Game Gallery as a channel.

0.10.n: The name portion of the speaker’s username Haru99.

0.11.n: These digits belong to the username Haru99; they do not indicate age or quantity here.

0.13.n: A polite ending used to introduce oneself; the speaker leaves out the word for I.

1.0.n: Tells when the speaker is introducing the item.

1.1.n: 紹介する means to introduce; ご adds respect toward the audience, and the phrase describes アイテム.

1.2.n: This borrowed English word refers to the game being presented.

1.3.n: Marks the item being introduced as what the sentence is about.

1.4.n: A polite way to point to the item being shown.

1.6.n: A spoken filler used while pausing before naming the game.

1.8.n: This is the game’s title, written in Japanese katakana.

1.10.n: Politely identifies the item as Artifacts, Inc.

1.11.n: Softens the introduction and invites the listener to follow along.

2.0.n: Sets the time frame for the planned unboxing review.

2.1.n: Makes 今日 the topic, setting up what the speaker will do today.

2.2.n: Here ですね provides a polite conversational pause rather than linking two things with is.

2.3.n: Pairs with です to gently hold the listener’s attention before continuing.

2.5.n: Refers to the game package being shown.

2.6.n: Links こちら to 中, indicating the inside of this package.

2.7.n: Refers to the interior or contents of the package.

2.8.n: Links the package’s contents to the unboxing review that follows.

2.9.n: Literally refers to opening a sealed package; it describes the kind of review.

2.10.n: Combines with 開封 to name the video’s format.

2.11.n: Marks the unboxing review as what the speaker wants to bring to the audience.

2.12.n: 届け is from 届ける; お届けする is a humble, polite way to speak of delivering something.

2.13.n: する becomes したい to express desire, completing お届けしたい.

2.14.n: Marks the preceding wish as the thought expressed by 思います.

2.15.n: Polite form of 思う; after たいと, it presents the speaker’s intention gently.

0.lit: Yes, The Game Gallery channel, Haru99 am.
0.tip: Japanese introductions often omit I; name + です politely identifies the speaker.

1.lit: Today introduce item, as for, this one, um, Artifacts, Inc. is, you see.
1.tip: 今日ご紹介する comes before アイテム to describe it: the item I’m introducing today.

2.lit: Today, as for, well, this’s inside’s unboxing review, to you bring want, that I think.
2.tip: 〜したいと思います is a polite, gentle way to announce what you would like to do.
